H6CA13199.name: Kyle Kirkland
H6CA13199.bio: Owner of Club One Casino in Fresno, president of the California Gaming Association, founder of the Kirkland Foundation, and former chairman of Steinway Musical Instruments.

positions.stance: Will "end over-regulation, restart domestic production, and attack the cost-of-living crisis head-on" to make housing, food, gas and healthcare affordable.
"Stop waste and fraud, demand audits, and require government to serve families—not itself—so every tax dollar delivers results."
"Give law enforcement the tools to stop fentanyl, human trafficking, and cartel violence while respecting legal immigration."
"Build storage, modernize delivery, and end the regulatory chokehold that hurts growers and farmworkers."
"Back the blue, support first responders, and end soft-on-crime policies that put families at risk."

H2CA20094.name: David Valadao
H2CA20094.bio: U.S. Representative and Central Valley dairy farmer who works on his family's farm in Kings County.

positions.stance: "It is critical to ensure California remains an agricultural leader that provides good careers for the Central Valley and food for the world."
Supports ensuring service members have tools to stay safe in battle, high-quality healthcare, and education and employment opportunities at home.
Says farmers, families and communities "must receive the water they need to strengthen the economy and raise our families."
Concerned that San Joaquin Valley unemployment is nearly double the national average and that too many district residents are out of work.
Believes "quality, affordable healthcare should be available to all Americans," including reforms that lower costs while protecting people with pre-existing conditions.

H6CA22190.name: Randy Villegas
H6CA22190.bio: College professor, mentor and community organizer from Kern County.

positions.stance: Wants to fight price gouging so families "pay a fair price to keep our families safe, and not a cent more."
Says healthcare is a human right and is "a strong supporter of Medicare for All."
Says any transition to renewable energy "must guarantee that all energy workers have well-paid, secure jobs and better wages."
Calls blanket detention and deportation unconstitutional; supports "a path to citizenship" for undocumented neighbors.
"I will fight to end corporate ownership of single-family homes"; supports a federal program to build affordable housing.

H0CA08135.name: Jay Obernolte
H0CA08135.bio: U.S. Representative for California's 23rd District, founder of software company FarSight Studios, former California State Assemblymember and former Mayor of Big Bear Lake.

positions.stance: Fighting "to balance the federal budget and stop the reckless spending that is driving inflation and increasing prices."
Says he fought to lower taxes, repeal gas taxes, provide small-business tax relief, and expand the child tax credit for working families.
Authored legislation to hold fentanyl dealers accountable and says he stopped the dumping of sexual predators in the community.
Fought to expand coverage for veterans exposed to toxic burn pits and is leading efforts to hold the VA accountable.
Voted to fully fund the military and to give troops a pay raise.

H6CA23230.name: Tessa Lynn Hodge
H6CA23230.bio: Licensed Clinical Social Worker with nearly a decade of experience working with vulnerable populations, including foster children and students needing mental health services.

positions.stance: "I will fight for a single-payer healthcare system so everyone gets the care they need, no exceptions."
Wants federal legislation and infrastructure investment to bring good-paying, skilled jobs to the 23rd District so residents can live and work locally.
Supports investing in diverse housing options, from affordable rentals to homeownership pathways: "no one should be priced out of the place they call home."
Supports reforms including "a clear pathway to legal status for long-term residents," protecting workers from exploitation, and keeping families together.
Will fight for stronger emission standards, federal funding for clean energy jobs, and protection of public lands like Joshua Tree.

H6CA24303.name: Salud Carbajal
H6CA24303.bio: U.S. Representative first elected in 2016 and a former U.S. Marine Corps Reserve member.

positions.stance: Works to ensure veterans get timely VA service, health care, jobs and education aid, and supports his Home for the Brave Act for homeless veterans.
"No one who works full time should live in poverty"; backed the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law to create good-paying union jobs.
"Lowering costs for you and your family is my number one priority in Congress."
Says it is "outrageous" that students take on crushing debt for college and pay higher interest rates than they should.
Says Congress should ensure "everyone can afford lifesaving care and medicine"; voted against repealing the Affordable Care Act.

H6CA24345.name: Bob Smith
H6CA24345.bio: Retired U.S. Navy Commander and combat veteran with 26 years of service and a systems engineering background.

positions.stance: "Cut wasteful spending, lower the cost of housing, energy, and food, and expand homeownership for working families."
"Reading, math, and STEM excellence, vocational pathways, and research partnerships with UCSB and Cal Poly."
"A balanced grid with reliable baseload power, coastline protection, and secure water storage and drought resilience."
"Secure the border, remove violent offenders, provide legal clarity for long term residents, and modernize agricultural and seasonal visas."
"Stop fentanyl at the source, lead in AI and cyber defense, and strengthen Vandenberg SFB and Naval Base Ventura County."

H2CA36439.name: Raul Ruiz
H2CA36439.bio: Emergency physician and U.S. Representative serving California's 25th District.

positions.stance: Will work "to expand and protect these commitments while opposing any cuts or changes to the retirement age."
Works to "cut bureaucratic red tape, level the playing field," help businesses thrive, and supports equal pay, paid leave and affordable child care.
Has voted against pay raises for Congress and wrote legislation barring members from using taxpayer money to fly first class.
Wrote and passed legislation providing health care access and improved benefits to veterans exposed to toxic substances such as burn pits.
Working to secure funding to address the Salton Sea, protect drinking water and air, and advance environmental justice and climate action.

H6CA25219.name: Joe Males
H6CA25219.bio: Marine Corps veteran, owner of a computer networking business since 1996, and Hemet City Council member.

H6CA26241.name: Sam Gallucci
H6CA26241.bio: Business executive, pastor who led Embrace! Church, and founder of four non-profits.

positions.stance: Says families are squeezed by housing, food, energy and insurance costs and "will fight to make Ventura County affordable for all."
Wants institutions to "thrive and re-earn trust through good faith reform."
Believes every child deserves a high-quality education and "holds parents' rights as his guiding principle in education."
Says what works is "treatment, housing tied to progress, and coordinated care."
Supports "a secure border and a legal, fair, humane system" and his proposed "National Settlement on Immigration."

H6CA26266.name: Jacqui Irwin
H6CA26266.bio: California Assemblymember first elected in 2014, former Mayor of Thousand Oaks, and former engineer at Teledyne Systems and Johns Hopkins University's Applied Physics Lab.

H4CA27111.name: George Whitesides
H4CA27111.bio: U.S. Representative for California's 27th District, former NASA Chief of Staff, former CEO of Virgin Galactic, and co-founder of Megafire Action.

positions.stance: Wants to grow local jobs, reduce commutes to Los Angeles, support small-business accelerator programs, and prioritize regional infrastructure projects.
Fighting "to lower your healthcare, housing, gas, and grocery bills" and to protect Social Security and Medicare.
Says everyone should be able to make reproductive health and abortion decisions "free from government interference"; cosponsors the Women's Health Protection Act.
Leading the charge to ban congressional stock trading and to bar officials from betting on world events they may have insider knowledge of.
Supports reducing wildland fuels, more firefighter resources, fire-detection technology, and help for fire-resistant home improvements to address the insurance crisis.

H6CA27306.name: Jason Gibbs
H6CA27306.bio: Santa Clarita City Council member (elected 2020, Mayor in 2023) and mechanical engineer who worked on Delta II, Delta IV and Atlas V rocket launch systems.

positions.stance: Will fight to lower the cost of living "by opposing new taxes, supporting energy affordability, and holding government accountable for wasteful spending."
Will support law enforcement, oppose "soft-on-crime" policies, and push to "end catch-and-release justice and restore consequences for criminal behavior."
Supports "securing the border, cracking down on fentanyl trafficking, and ending policies that reward illegal entry"; believes in legal immigration.
Believes local communities, not state or federal politicians, know best how to manage housing, schools and public safety; opposes one-size-fits-all mandates.
Will fight for "opportunity, transparency, and high standards" and expand career pathways and technical training; says parents deserve a say in what's taught.

H0CA32101.name: Judy Chu
H0CA32101.bio: U.S. Representative since 2009 and member of the House Ways and Means Committee.

H4CA28127.name: April Verlato
H4CA28127.bio: Former Mayor of Arcadia, businesswoman and attorney.

positions.stance: Opposes "burdensome regulations that stifle growth" and will fight to create "a climate that brings good-paying jobs and economic vitality back."
Supports better mental health and substance abuse treatment, cutting red tape that delays funding, and local solutions like the San Gabriel Valley Regional Housing Trust Fund.
Says it is "the government's duty to protect its citizens" from drug trafficking and terrorism; advocates stronger border security and supporting law enforcement.
Supports controlling mandatory spending and opposing tax increases; a proponent of the Taxpayer Protection Pledge.
Supports a stronger military and energy independence, and wants more veteran clinics and a major medical center in the San Gabriel Valley.

H4CA29141.name: Luz Rivas
H4CA29141.bio: U.S. Representative for California's 29th District elected in 2025, former California State Assemblymember, electrical engineer, and founder of the nonprofit DIY Girls.

H8CA29100.name: Angelica Dueñas
H8CA29100.bio: Community organizer and former two-term President of the Sun Valley Area Neighborhood Council.

positions.stance: Supports "housing as a fundamental right"; aims to combat gentrification, advocate for affordable homes, and end homelessness.
"Advocating for Medicare for All, promoting a single-payer solution" to reform the current healthcare system.
"Any loan backed by stock should be treated and taxed as income, just like wages."
Advocates "a foreign policy of peace, prosperity, and collaboration through diplomacy, human rights, fair trade, and responsible military spending."
Champions "legal status for all, DREAM Act citizenship, work visa programs, healthcare access, and justice for asylum seekers."

H4CA30149.name: Laura Friedman
H4CA30149.bio: U.S. Representative for California's 30th District, former State Assemblymember, and former Glendale City Council member and Mayor.

H6CA30250.name: Scott Meyers
H6CA30250.bio: Attorney who has practiced civil law for 37 years.

positions.stance: Opposes "reckless federal spending that fuels inflation"; supports lower taxes, American energy independence, and cutting regulatory red tape on housing and small business.
Supports securing the southern border, aggressive enforcement against drug trafficking, and law enforcement; opposes "sanctuary policies that undermine public safety."
Wants transparency for taxpayer dollars, including using federal leverage over California's high-speed rail project and exposing wasteful homelessness spending.
Wants to restore focus on "reading, writing, math, and analytical thinking," opposes political indoctrination in classrooms, and supports parental rights.
Wants to make California competitive again for film and television production and keep American entertainment jobs in America.

H2CA39151.name: Eric Ching
H2CA39151.bio: Business owner for 30 years and former Mayor of Walnut who served three terms on the Walnut City Council.

positions.stance: Will support First Amendment freedoms, "our rights to keep and bear arms," and protection from unreasonable searches and seizures.
Will promote legal trade and tourism while supporting ways to secure the border "from the illegal movement of weapons, drugs, contraband, and people."
Will support laws promoting transparency and honesty, reasonable compensation for officials, and "term limits for federal, state, and local officials."
Supports being tough on crime through deterrence, restitution to victims, and holding accountable officials "who selectively neglect to do their jobs."
Supports school choice and high standards; "will oppose any identity-based entrance policies or racially divisive material" in school curriculums.

H6CA24113.name: Brad Sherman
H6CA24113.bio: U.S. Representative, senior member of the House Foreign Affairs and Financial Services Committees, and former CPA who headed the California Board of Equalization.

positions.stance: Cosponsors bills including an Assault Weapons Ban and background check legislation, and "remains committed to working on a bipartisan basis to see these bills signed into law."
Working to help disabled veterans facing homelessness, including through his Housing Unhoused Disabled Veterans Act, and to secure funds for veteran supportive housing.
Cosponsored the Green New Deal and supports "establishing a national emergency for climate change" with a whole-of-government approach.
Working to pass the SAFE Act "to end the practice of horse slaughter for good" and strongly opposes efforts to undermine California's Proposition 12.
Advocates strengthening the U.S.-Israel relationship and fully funding the Iron Dome and the annual $3.8 billion in aid under the 2016 MOU.

H4CA32137.name: Larry Thompson
H4CA32137.bio: Entertainment lawyer, talent manager, film producer, author and motivational speaker.

positions.stance: "I believe in the peaceful transfer of power for every Presidential election."
"I stand tall with Israel and all Jews worldwide. Period."
"Keep the damn thing closed"; deport those here illegally and govern by existing immigration laws.
Personally against abortion but says it is an issue for the states; "I also do not believe in a federal law banning a woman's right to choose."
"I am very tough on crime"; supports police and prosecuting criminals "according to the letter and spirit of the law."

H2CA31125.name: Pete Aguilar
H2CA31125.bio: U.S. Representative for California's 33rd District since 2014, Chair of the House Democratic Caucus, and former Mayor of Redlands.

H6CA33114.name: Stephanie Vargas
H6CA33114.bio: Chief Deputy City Clerk for the City of Colton and former charter school board chair.

positions.stance: "I stand firmly behind the enforcement of our laws and the removal of dangerous criminals from our communities."
Supports "the common-sense approach to forest management" and giving fire officials authority to use every available prevention strategy.
Wants to restore "fiscal sanity," drive down living and energy costs, remove bureaucratic barriers, and ensure accountability for fraud at taxpayers' expense.
Supports incentivizing affordable single-family home construction through voluntary partnerships and using federal surplus land, rather than unfunded mandates on local governments.
"I will vote to stop bans on American energy"; says producing more oil and gas at home lowers fuel and heating costs.

H8CA34266.name: Jimmy Gomez
H8CA34266.bio: U.S. Representative, educator, renters' advocate and former union organizer.

positions.stance: Fights to pass Medicare for All "so no one goes without health care"; an original cosponsor of the Medicare for All Act.
"Abortion is a fundamental right"; will fight to ensure access to abortion is "once again" the law of the land.
Fights to make housing more affordable and protect renters; proposes affordable starter homes and up to $50,000 in down payment assistance for first-time buyers.
Champions legislation for affordable childcare, paid family leave and the enhanced child tax credit to lower costs for families.
Committed to raising the minimum wage and securing worker and union protections, and says billionaires must pay their fair share in taxes.

H6CA34286.name: Angela Gonzales-Torres
H6CA34286.bio: Community organizer and equity and justice advocate from Los Angeles.

positions.stance: Refuses corporate and Super PAC money and is fighting "to abolish Super PACs, overturn Citizens United" and limit contractor campaign funding.
Supports "a federal housing system built on vouchers as a guarantee, community land trusts, and permanently affordable housing."
Supports a Guaranteed Basic Income pilot, the right to unionize for gig workers, and real paid leave and childcare support.
"Healthcare is a human right"; will co-sponsor Medicare for All, cancel medical debt, and break up healthcare monopolies.
Supports "a federal wealth tax to make the ultra-rich pay their fair share" and fund housing, healthcare and education.

H4CA35031.name: Norma Torres
H4CA35031.bio: U.S. Representative for California's 35th District, former Mayor, and former 911 emergency dispatcher.

positions.stance: Committed to connecting communities and creating good-paying jobs through reliable transportation infrastructure, expanded public transit, and electric vehicle infrastructure.
Says she "strongly believes that health care is a human right"; fighting to strengthen the Affordable Care Act and restore Medicaid services.
Dedicated to helping veterans receive the benefits they're owed and expanding their access to education and health care.
Working to ensure students have the tools to succeed from preschool to college, including funding college students' basic needs through her BASIC Act.
Committed to "tackling the climate crisis head-on," improving public transit, modernizing energy systems, and holding polluters accountable.

H0CA35146.name: Mike Cargile
H0CA35146.bio: Former U.S. Army officer and co-founder of the San Bernardino County Patriots and the Tri-County Sheriff's Forum.

positions.stance: Says he "stridently stands against" open borders, citing human trafficking, fentanyl and lost American jobs; supports the right to self-defense.
Opposes "boys in girls' sports," DEI and CRT, and supports the right of parents "to know EVERYTHING that goes on in school."
Says he "will protect the gas in your car, the gas in your stove, the price of the food on your table and the safety of your family."
Stands with law enforcement and first responders and supports qualified immunity for officers.
Says seniors are "the most used and abused demographic in our country," courted by politicians at election time and then neglected.

H4CA33119.name: Ted Lieu
H4CA33119.bio: U.S. Representative for California's 36th District, Vice Chair of the House Democratic Caucus, and veteran.
